thread:
junaid: heads-up — after last night's kernel+driver push in us-west-2 we started seeing A100s drop P2P and report reduced BAR1 mappings. NVLink peers failing during NCCL init on ~8 hosts across rack-7 and rack-9. most jobs hit allreduce hangs.
ops-bot: deploy finished: kernel-5.16.18 + nvidia-driver-535.54.03 pushed to us-west-2 @ 2026-03-01T03:14Z (canary 10% -> 100%).
maria: confirming — dmesg snippet from host gpu-07-9: 
```
[   12.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=2389, GPU has fallen off the bus
[   12.345683] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: 0000:65:00.0
[   12.345689] nvidia: peer access disabled: PCI ACS virtualization present -> BAR1 map truncated
```
janaid: thanks. the "peer access disabled" line matches what we see in telemetry — kernel reports ACS capability present, so Linux is isolating BAR1 windows.
felix: probable root cause: newer upstream kernel enables PCIe ACS routing/patches + NVIDIA driver 535 changed BAR1 negotiation. when ACS is enforced some devices cannot access peers directly -> NCCL falls back but our fallback wasn't triggered reliably.
sre-oncall: impact? how many customers/jobs? any dedicated clusters affected? :rotating_light:
maria: current tally: ~8 hosts overloaded, ~24 running jobs affected in us-west-2-prod (mix of hosted and a couple dedicated pools). latency increases and some OOMs from retries. No private VPC customers reported yet.
janaid: cost note — queuing/bounces caused autoscaler to spin up ephemeral Ampere nodes earlier, tacking on ~$4k extra this billing window.
felix: short-term mitigation — we can force driver to expose legacy BAR1 mapping on affected nodes by reverting driver packaging to 525 and keeping kernel 5.15 ABI, or enable NVreg peer-to-peer flags if available. trying safe option: restart kube-node with nvidia module param NVreg_EnablePeerToPeer=1 to see if peer access reappears.
maria: also validated that setting PCIe ACS override on kernel cmdline (pci=pcie_acs_force_disable) on a single canary node restored P2P + NCCL init succeeded. reproducer steps in INC-2026.
sre-oncall: do not mass-flip ACS kernel flags without engineering approval — that affects isolation model and security review. We need a rollback plan for the fleet upgrade.
janaid: agreed. propose rollback of driver to 525 on the 100 nodes in us-west-2 that got the rollout, keep kernel as-is for now and stop the driver rollout. this should restore previous BAR1 sizes and P2P. deploy-bot: rollback runbook available: `scripts/driver-rollback.sh --version 525 --region us-west-2` (dry-run first).
felix: I'll start a bisection to find minimal change: is it kernel A, driver B, or their interaction. plan: 1) repro on one node with driver-525 + kernel-5.16 2) driver-535 + kernel-5.15 3) driver-535 + kernel-5.16. this will isolate which component introduced the ACS/BAR1 regression.
maria: created INC-2026 and linked to RFD-834 for change control. tagging dedicated-customer-impacted.
sre-oncall: action items:
- stop driver rollout in pipeline (jenkins job #2123) — @deploy-bot please hold.
- schedule emergency rollback for 100 nodes, target window 04:30-05:30 UTC.
- Felix to run bisection on a spare host and post results to thread.
- Maria to open billing ticket for the autoscaler overspend.
janaid: i'll coordinate the rollback and notify customer-success for the dedicated pools. will include mitigations and follow-up postmortem.
felix: quick note on workaround we tested: adding kernel cmdline `pci=pcie_acs_override=0x0` (canary-only) restored BAR1 mapping — but this is distro/kernel specific and not acceptable long-term. needs driver/kernel vendor fix.
maria: logs/telemetry saved to s3://redwood-ops/incident/1775234500/. NCCL traces, nvidia-smi -q outputs, and dmesg archived.
sre-oncall: assigning oncall to the incident — @sre-oncall will lead until resolved. escalate to vendor if bisection points to driver.
janaid: thanks everyone. will update when rollback starts. :thumbsup:
